To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity-guided fraction of the Cyclopie nutraceutical extract, SM6Met yielded three fractions with the desired estrogenic attributes separated into different fractions, with only F3 displaying robust ERβ agonism.
the activity-guided fraction of SM6Met, F3, displays robust ERβ agonism and also antagonizes E2-induced breast cell proliferation.

the desirable estrogenic activity profile of SM6Met can be fractionated and that this fractionation results in separation of the previously described positive estrogenic attributes, with the exception of the ERα antagonist activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of compounds from SM6Met with the aim of identifying a lead compound with the potential of being developed into a phytoestrogeneic nutraceutical.
the development of a phytopharmaceutical that can be used to treat menopausal symptoms and breast cancer.
the isolation and identification of the active constituents of the Cyclopio nutraceutical extract, SM6Met and the elucidation of their mechanisms of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the desirable estrogenic properties of SM6Met are not the result of a synergistic interaction of the individual polyphenols in the NPF of SM6Met but rather the result of an additive effect of these polyphenols.
the desirable estrogenic properties of the SM6Met nutraceutical extract could not be replicated in the fractions obtained from activity-guided fractionations.
fractionation may not be the optimal approach for future development of the SM6Met phytoestrogen nutraceutical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the original extract SM6Met, as well as its HPCCC fraction F3, are promising nutraceutical leads.
the optimal approach may be to retain the polyphenolic diversity in the original extract.
the original SM6 Met extract displays the desirable estrogenic properties, but that the optimal approach to retain these properties is to use a combination of the HPCCC fractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of polyphenols may be required to confer the desired estrogenic profile to the SM6Met extract.

the original SM6met extract should be used as a starting point to develop a nutraceutical, and that the desirable estrogenic activities of the original extract should be retained in a single fraction.
the desirable estrogenic activities of SM6Met are not confined to one polyphenolic class or group of polyphenols.
